, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 4  MFA No.200962/2015  c/w MFA CROB NO.200064/2015  JUDGMENT

These two appeals filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('the Act' for short) are directed against the impugned judgment and award dated 18.04.2015 in MVC.No.100/2011 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Humnabad, whereby though the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.6,70,200/- with interest at 6% p.a.,
it has dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.3-Insurance Company and directed respondent Nos.1 and 2 being the driver and owner of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA- 39/5166 ('the offending vehicle' for short) to pay the same.
2.

While MFA.No.2009626/2015 is filed by respondent No.2-owner of the offending vehicle,
MFA.Crob.No.200064/2018 is filed by the petitioner seeking enhancement of the compensation as well as to direct respondent No.3-Insurance Company to pay the same.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioner that on 12.08.2008 at 12.00 noon, for business purpose, he had gone to Sadashivpet.

While he was proceeding on the left side of the road, opposite to Sangam Hotel, respondent No.1 being the driver of the offending vehicle, drove the same in a rash or Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90188325/
3 negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.

entities.text: Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner fell down on the road and the tyre ran over his right leg knee.
As a result of accidental injuries, his left leg was amputated below the knee level.
Despite prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured and sustained permanent partial disability affecting his income.

As the driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle,
respondents were liable to pay compensation with interest and prays to allow the petition.

5. After due service of notice, respondents appeared through their counsel and filed separate written statement denying and disputing that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
They have disputed the age, occupation and income of the petitioner and that the accidental injuries resulted in permanent partial disability.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have contended that as at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.3, it is liable to pay compensation.
6. On the other hand, respondent No.3 has specifically contended that at the time of accident, the petitioner was traveling in the offending vehicle.
He tried to get down from the vehicle by stepping on the tyre and fell down and sustained injuries.

Since he was the gratuitous passenger, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and as such, respondent No.3 is not liable to pay compensation and prays to dismiss the petition as against it.
7. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
8. In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and the Doctor, who has issued the disability certificate as PW-2.

He has relied upon Exs.P-1 to P-11.
9.

Respondents have not lead any oral evidence, but insurance policy is marked as Ex.R-1.
10.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that at the time of accident, petitioner was traveling in the offending vehicle as a gratuitous passenger and as such, respondent No.3 is not liable to indemnify respondent No.2.

After considering the evidence of PW-2, it held that petitioner has sustained permanent partial disability to the extent of 60% to the whole body and quantified the compensation at Rs.6,70,200/- and directed respondent Nos.1 and 2 to pay the same with interest at 6% p.a. as detailed below:
Heads Amount  In Rs.
Medical expenses 1,00,000  Loss of income 5,61,600  Traveling and other expenses 5,000
Medical attendants 3,600

11. Petitioner has challenged the impugned Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90188325/
4 judgment and award contending that the compensation awarded is on the lower side.

entities.text: Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head 'loss of future prospects', 'Pain and Suffering', 'Loss of income during laid up period', and 'Loss of amenities of life as well as for artificial limb.
The income ought to have been taken at Rs.9,000/- per month as against Rs.6,000/- considered by the Tribunal.

12. On the other hand, respondent No.2 has challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that the Tribunal has erred in holding that petitioner was an unauthorized passenger in the offending vehicle and thereby absolving respondent No.3 from the liability.
The evidence placed on record indicate that at the time of accident, petitioner was moving on the road, when the offending vehicle came and dashed against him.
The income taken at Rs.6,000/- per month is on the higher side.
The compensation granted under the other heads is also on the higher side and prays to allow the appeal and reduce the compensation and fasten the liability on respondent No.3.

13. On the other hand, learned counsel representing respondent No.3-Insurance Company supported the impugned judgment and award and submitted that appreciating the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, the Tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion that petitioner was an unauthorized passenger traveling in the offending vehicle and thereby absolved respondent No.3 and prays to dismiss both appeals.

14. Heard arguments of both sides and perused the record.
15.

So far as the contention of respondent No.3 that petitioner had traveled in the offending vehicle and while getting down from lorry, he fell down and sustained injuries is concerned, respondent No.3 has relied upon the complaint averments at Ex.P-2.
This complaint is lodged by one Thota Mallanna stated to be an acquaintance of the petitioner.
However, petitioner has denied that he knew the complainant.

Except averments in the complaint, there is no other material to show that at the time of accident, petitioner had traveled in the offending vehicle and while getting down from the same, he slipped and sustained injury.
At least respondent No.3 could have examined the complainant to prove the contents of the complaint.

16. In the absence of any oral evidence to support the contents of the complaint, respondent No.3 has failed to prove that immediately prior the accident, petitioner had traveled in the offending vehicle and while getting down, he slipped and sustained injury.
It is not clear that whether the complainant has also traveled with the petitioner in the said lorry or in what way he was able to come to know that petitioner has traveled in the offending vehicle.

The examination of the complainant would have clarified this aspect and supported the contention of respondent No.3 that petitioner was an unauthorized passenger in the offending vehicle and while getting down, he fell down and sustained injuries.
In the absence of such supporting evidence, this Court is of the considered opinion that the contents of compliant are not sufficient to prove the said allegation.

17. Of course the Tribunal as well as this Court cannot expect respondent Nos.1 and 2 being the driver and owner of the offending vehicle would step into the witness box to speak that at the time of accident, petitioner had traveled in the offending vehicle as unauthorized passenger.

Therefore,
Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90188325/
5 complainant was the proper person to speak with regard to the averment that immediately prior to the accident, petitioner had traveled in the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the absence of his evidence, this Court is of the considered opinion that there is no material to hold that petitioner was an unauthorized passenger in the offending vehicle and therefore, respondent No.3 is not liable to pay the compensation.

18. In the light of the above discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Tribunal has erred in coming to the conclusion that petitioner was an unauthorized passenger in the offending vehicle and as such, respondent No.3 is not liable to pay the compensation.
Consequently, the findings of the Tribunal to that effect is liable to be set aside.
19. Now coming to the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal for the injury sustained by the petitioner in the accident involving the offending vehicle.
20. Loss of income due to disability: Indisputably, due to the injury suffered by the petitioner, his left leg is amputated below the knee level.
Considering the evidence of PW-2, the Tribunal has come to a correct conclusion that the disability is to the extent of 60% of the whole body.
Based on the record, the Tribunal has correctly accepted the age of the petitioner as 50 years.

In the absence of evidence to prove the exact income, though the Tribunal is justified in considering the income of the petitioner on notional basis, having regard to the fact that accident is of the year 2008, based on minimum wages, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.4,250/- per month as against Rs.6,000/- considered by the Tribunal.

Therefore, the notional income is considered at Rs.4,250/-
per month.
Having regard to the fact that petitioner has sustained 60% of the disability, it would be appropriate to add 'loss of future prospects' which the Tribunal has failed to consider.

Having regard to the fact that at the time of accident, petitioner was aged about 50 years, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Ors1, 25% of the income is required to be (2018) 18 SCC 130 added towards loss of future prospects.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Ors1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, notional income of the petitioner is required to be taken at Rs.5,312/-.
With the age of the petitioner as 50 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 13.
With these components, the compensation under head 'loss of income due to disability' is Rs.5,312/- x 12 x 13 x 60% = Rs.4,97,203/- as against Rs.5,61,600/- granted by the Tribunal.
21. Medical expenses:

Though the petitioner has failed to produce any medical bills, having regard to the fact that due to the injury sustained by the petitioner, he had undergone amputation, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head 'Medical expenses' and the same is confirmed.
22. Traveling and other expenses:
However, the compensation granted in a sum of Rs.5,000/- under the head 'traveling and other expenses' is on the lower side and the same is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.

Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90188325/
6 23.

entities.text: Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Medical attendant charges:
Similarly, the compensation granted under the head 'medical attendant charges' in a sum of Rs.3,600/- is on the lower side and the same is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
24. Loss of income during laid up period:
The Tribunal has not at all granted any compensation under the head 'Loss of income during laid up period'.

Having regard to the fact that the petitioner had undergone amputation of the left leg below the knee level, it would be reasonable to expect that he was under treatment atleast for a period of six months.

At the rate of Rs.4,250/- for a period of six months, petitioner is entitled to compensation in a sum of Rs.25,500/- under the head 'Loss of income during laid up period'.
25. Pain and Suffering and Loss of amenities of life:
The Tribunal has not at all granted any compensation under the head 'Pain and Suffering' and 'Loss of amenities of life'.

Taking into consideration the fact that the injury sustained by the petitioner has resulted in amputation of his left leg below the knee level, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head 'Pain and Suffering' and Rs.40,000/- under the head 'Loss of amenities of life'.
26.
For artificial Limb: The Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head 'For artificial Limb'.
However, the petitioner has not at all produced any material to show as to what exactly would be the expenses for the artificial limb.

Anyhow, taking into consideration the date of the accident and other attending circumstances, it would be reasonable to grant a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head 'For artificial Limb'.
27.
Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.7,82,703/- as against Rs.6,70,200/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

 in Rs.

Medical expenses 1,00,000 1,00,000  Loss of income 5,61,600 4,97,203  Traveling and other 5,000 10,000  expenses  Medical attendant 3,600 10,000  charges  Loss of income during - 25,500  laid up period  Pain and Suffering - 50,000  Loss of amenities of - 40,000  life  For artificial Limb - 50,000 Tukkappa S/O Bakkappa Helva vs Chandrakant S/O Madeppa Kabbaliga on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90188325/
7  TOTAL 6,70,200 7,82,703 28.
Admittedly, at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was covered by valid policy issued by respondent No.3-Insurance Company.

Since respondent No.3 has failed to prove that petitioner was an unauthorized traveler in the offending vehicle, it cannot escape its liability from paying the compensation and as such, the impugned judgment and award so far as exonerating respondent No.3 from paying the compensation is liable to be set aside

and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
( a) MFA No.200962/2015 and MFA Crob No.200064/2015 filed by respondent No.2/owner of the offending vehicle as well as petitioner
are allowed.

(b) The impugned judgment and award so far as exonerating respondent No.3/Insurance Company from liability of paying the compensation is set aside (c) The compensation is enhanced to Rs.7,82,703/- as against Rs.6,70,200/- granted by the Tribunal.

(d) Respondent No.3/Insurance Company is directed to pay compensation together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(e) The amount in deposit in MFA No.200962/2015 (by respondent No.2) is permitted to be withdrawn by him.
(f) The Registry is directed to send back the trial Court records along with copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.

Sd/-
